source.title: Learning Stages: Phenomenon, Root Cause, Mechanism Hypothesis, and Implications
source.authors: Kai-Chao You; Mingsheng Long; Michael I. Jordan; Jian-Min Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper “How Does Learning Rate Decay Help Modern Neural Networks?”, not the titled study “Learning Stages: Phenomenon, Root Cause, Mechanism Hypothesis, and Implications.”
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether learning-rate conditions affect fitting noisy examples in a constructed dataset, a component of V4, using a different setup from the original random-label studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a 10% noisy-data experiment on PS10. It does not test fully random labels, unstructured inputs, or the claim versions about training time, regularization, or learning real labels before random labels.
record.test_reason: Section 5.3 measures fitting noisy training examples under two learning-rate schedules, bearing on V4's noise-memorization component. It does not establish the full corruption-dependent claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that an initially large learning rate suppresses noisy-data memorization, while learning-rate decay improves learning of complex patterns. They also report decreasing transferability of additional patterns learned in later stages.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a constructed pattern-separation dataset with 10% noise and compares learning-rate schedules; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different noise-data accuracy behavior for large lr with decay versus keeping the learning rate small.

fits_no_version.finding: On PS10, simple patterns are learned quickly and complex-pattern accuracy improves after learning-rate decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate magnitude affects which pattern complexities a network learns.

fits_no_version.finding: Additional patterns learned in later training stages transfer less well across datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The transferability of additional learned patterns decreases across learning-rate-decay stages.

record.problems: The relevant noise result is shown only in a figure, with no numeric values or uncertainty stated in the text; the setup uses a constructed dataset and only 10% noise.
record.rows_left_out: No other results directly test the listed versions. Results about simple and complex pattern accuracy and transferability do not measure the behaviors named by those versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without changing hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios for true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption sweep from none to all, perfect training fit at each fraction, and steadily increasing test error toward chance. The noisy-data generation procedure is unspecified.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and generalization without these regularizers.
The supplied readable text does not establish that real-label learning precedes noisy-label memorization. Simple-before-complex learning alone does not test that ordering.

missing.what: Figure 10 also reports simple- and complex-pattern accuracy over training alongside noisy-data accuracy. These trajectories are needed to assess V6 directly; their ordering cannot be recovered from the supplied text. The blanket rows_left_out statement overlooks this potentially relevant comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied study is titled How Does Learning Rate Decay Help Modern Neural Networks? The alleged alternative title appears only in the record. No source-identity mismatch can be resolved from this message. Exact curve values and temporal ordering are unavailable; lower noisy-data accuracy must not be equated with absent memorization.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training/test error, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time and convergence as corruption fraction changes are not tested.
Shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
Only a 10% noisy-data condition is studied; the paper does not report perfect training accuracy, test error, or a sweep from no corruption to all labels corrupted.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their effect on random-label fitting or true-label generalization are not tested.
The paper does not compare learning real labels with learning random labels over training.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on PS10 with 10% noisy data using a large learning rate with decay; noise-data accuracy was plotted.
rows.note: The text says an initially large learning rate suppresses fitting noisy data; no numeric accuracy is given in the text.
rows.check: The text establishes less noisy-data fitting than R2, but the supplied figure extraction contains no readable curves or endpoint values. Relative suppression alone cannot establish whether fitting is partial, absent, or eventually complete. The construction of the noisy data, including whether labels were randomly corrupted, is unspecified.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on PS10 with 10% noisy data using a constant small learning rate; noise-data accuracy was plotted.
rows.note: Compared with large lr with decay; the text describes the latter as suppressing noisy-data fitting, but reports no exact values.
rows.check: The text establishes more noisy-data fitting than R1, but provides no readable accuracy or endpoint. The original partial state is unsupported. R1 is the schedule comparator; neither row has a reported numerical baseline.

relationships.condition: WideResNet on PS10 with 10% noisy data; initially large learning rate with decay versus a constant small learning rate
relationships.reason: Section 5.3 explicitly attributes reduced noisy-data fitting to the initially large learning rate (R1–R2), showing schedule dependence of memorization; it does not establish failure of eventual perfect fit.
relationships.display_finding: Starting with a large learning rate reduced noisy-data fitting relative to a constant small learning rate.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
